issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodos function - Direct string interpolation of user input into SQL query using template literal
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with $1 placeholder instead of string concatenation. Replace with: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $1'; const searchPattern = `%${keyword}%`; await db.query(query, [searchPattern]);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus function - Direct string concatenation of user input into SQL query
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with $1 placeholder. Replace with: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; await db.query(query, [completed]);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser function - Direct string interpolation of userId into SQL query with template literal
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with $1 placeholder. Replace with: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Incorrect parameter type in searchTodosByStatus - Parameter should be boolean, not string, which can lead to type coercion errors
issues.suggestion: Change the parameter type from 'string' to 'boolean' for type safety: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]>

issues.description: LIKE queries with leading wildcards prevent index usage and can cause performance issues on large datasets
issues.suggestion: Consider using full-text search capabilities or add pagination parameters (limit, offset) to prevent loading excessive data. Document performance implications for large datasets.

issues.description: Missing input validation - No validation that keyword is non-empty or has reasonable length limits
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!keyword?.trim()) { return []; } to prevent unnecessary database queries and potential DoS attacks with extremely long strings

issues.description: Missing input validation in getTodosByUser - userId should be validated to ensure it's a valid format
issues.suggestion: Add validation to ensure userId is non-empty and matches expected format (e.g., UUID or numeric pattern)

codeQuality.summary: The code has three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities that must be addressed immediately. All three new search functions use unsafe string concatenation/interpolation instead of parameterized queries, directly violating the secure patterns used elsewhere in the file (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo all use parameterized queries). Additional issues include incorrect type usage (string instead of boolean), missing input validation, and performance concerns with LIKE queries.

testCoverage.summary: All three new search functions have ZERO test coverage. The existing test file (src/todo.test.ts) only covers validateTodoInput and sanitizeInput functions. Critical gaps include: no SQL injection security tests (despite vulnerabilities in code), no input validation tests, no edge case handling (null/undefined/empty strings), no case-sensitivity verification, and no JOIN operation tests for getTodosByUser. The complete absence of tests combined with critical security vulnerabilities makes this code unsafe for production deployment.

suggestions.description: Replace SQL injection vulnerability by using parameterized queries consistent with existing secure patterns in the file
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates critical SQL injection vulnerability by using parameterized queries with $1, $2 placeholders. Aligns with existing secure patterns used in createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, and deleteTodo functions. Prevents attackers from executing arbitrary SQL commands through malicious keyword input.

suggestions.description: Replace SQL injection vulnerability and fix incorrect parameter type to boolean
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates SQL injection vulnerability and improves type safety by using boolean instead of string. Prevents boolean-based blind SQL injection attacks. Makes function signature more self-documenting and prevents invalid string values. Maintains consistency with codebase security patterns.

suggestions.description: Replace SQL injection vulnerability in JOIN query with parameterized query
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates SQL injection vulnerability in JOIN query by using parameterized query with $1 placeholder. Prevents unauthorized data access through SQL injection in the JOIN clause. Ensures consistency with existing secure query patterns throughout the file.

suggestions.benefits: Prevents unnecessary database queries for invalid input. Improves performance by short-circuiting empty searches. Provides consistent behavior for edge cases. Trims whitespace to improve search accuracy and prevent whitespace-only searches.

suggestions.after: export async function searchTodosByUserId(userId: string): Promise<Todo[]>

refactorings.summary: Three critical security refactorings required immediately: all new search functions must replace string concatenation/interpolation with parameterized queries using the $1, $2 placeholder pattern already established in the codebase. The searchTodosByStatus function additionally needs its parameter type changed from string to boolean. These changes align with existing secure patterns in createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, and deleteTodo. Additional improvements include input validation and consistent naming.

recommendations.description: Immediately fix all three SQL injection vulnerabilities by replacing string concatenation/interpolation with parameterized queries. All three functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) directly inject user input into SQL queries, allowing arbitrary SQL execution. The codebase already has the correct pattern in other functions (createTodo, getTodoById, etc.) using $1, $2 placeholders - apply the same pattern here.

Add comprehensive test coverage for all three new search functions. Currently 0% of the new functionality is tested. Critical tests needed: SQL injection prevention, input validation (null/undefined/empty), edge cases, case sensitivity, and JOIN integrity for getTodosByUser. Without tests, the security vulnerabilities cannot be verified as fixed.

Fix searchTodosByStatus parameter type from string to boolean. The completed status is a boolean concept and should be typed accordingly to prevent invalid values ('yes', 'maybe', etc.) and improve type safety. This also requires updating the SQL query to handle boolean values correctly.

Add input validation to all three search functions. Validate that keyword is non-empty and within reasonable length limits, that completed is a valid boolean value (if keeping as string), and that userId is in expected format. This prevents unnecessary database queries and potential DoS attacks.

Consider adding pagination support to all search functions to prevent loading excessive data. LIKE queries with leading wildcards cannot use indexes efficiently. Add limit/offset parameters or consider full-text search capabilities for better performance on large datasets.
